visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The host, a middle-aged male with glasses wearing a black shirt, stands in a snowy urban street at night. He holds a light blue pen in his right hand and a black clicker in his left. The background features a multi-story building with illuminated windows and trees laden with fresh snow, creating a crisp night environment. (2) A rectangular inset appears showing an elderly woman with short silver hair. She is wearing large pink over-ear headphones and a simple white blouse. She smiles contentedly with her eyes closed, standing on a beach where gentle waves and sand are visible under bright daylight. (3) The host returns to the full vertical frame, gesturing dynamically with both hands to emphasize his verbal points. The snowy background remains static, and the lighting on his face is balanced, suggesting a controlled outdoor shoot or a high-quality green screen effect. (4) A digital overlay showing the header of a scientific journal 'JNeurosci' (The Journal of Neuroscience) appears over the host's chest. Below it, technical text regarding age-related positivity bias in emotion recognition and brain connectivity changes is displayed in a formal academic format. (5) A grid of four facial images showing the same man with ambiguous, slightly smiling expressions is overlaid on the screen. The host continues to speak while the images illustrate the concept of blended or ambiguous emotional states used in the research study. (6) Four brain MRI slices (labeled A, B, C, D) are shown alongside a scatter plot with blue and red dots. Red circles highlight specific areas in the brain scans, specifically the amygdala and hippocampal regions, to demonstrate the correlation between gray matter volume and positivity bias. (7) The host is shown in a medium full shot, continuing his explanation. He makes circular motions with the pen and clicker. Yellow variety captions appear at the top and bottom of the screen to highlight key takeaways before the video concludes.
